ACC-0001.explanation: Invoice is 21 days overdue with 2 failed payments in 90 days, and an open ticket shows confusion over a pending card authorization differing from the invoice. Usage is only mildly softer, so a billing follow-up should resolve it.

ACC-0002.explanation: Usage is steady, billing is clean and tickets are routine closed how-to questions. Repeated audit-log question is informational only.

ACC-0003.explanation: Downgrade requested and an overdue notice is open, but the customer says they paid by bank transfer so the overdue status may be a reconciliation error. Usage is strong, though the last CSM contact was 114 days ago.

ACC-0004.explanation: At 3 months only account setup is done (no integration, team invite, workflow or report) and there are three open tickets, including a quick-start screen mismatch. Usage is rising, so a guided onboarding playbook should recover this.

ACC-0005.explanation: Customer asks for someone with authority to call after four weeks of back-and-forth on the same integration error and complains about repeated canned macros. Emotionally charged support failure despite stable usage.

ACC-0006.explanation: Invoice is 48 days overdue with a failed payment, but the open ticket says they need to move billing to a new card and contact, which explains it. Help update payment details; usage is small but flat.

ACC-0007.explanation: Usage dipped from roughly 120 to about 40 but is recovering to 77, and the CSM note attributes it to an accreditation review with the contact promising to reach out. Billing is clean, so treat it as a temporary dip.

ACC-0008.explanation: Usage is stable and billing is clean. Open token ticket is minor and already resolved by the customer.

ACC-0009.explanation: Usage is steady and healthy, and the customer asked for a call to plan rollout to a second location 51 days ago with no recorded follow-up. This is an expansion opportunity needing a human.

ACC-0010.explanation: Weekly sessions collapsed from about 160 to 23 over six months across 33 seats, with no CSM contact for 68 days. The CSM note about renewal paperwork contradicts the usage trend, so a human should verify.

ACC-0011.explanation: Usage dropped to about half, but the CSM note says the customer warned of a cutover and low logins. The CRM comparison email says the tool stays, so it is not competitive. Do check in as the planned follow-up is overdue.

ACC-0012.explanation: Usage is stable, billing clean and CSM reports no impact from the update. The new expense tool only feeds uploads into the platform, and the customer asked for beta access.

ACC-0013.explanation: New account (2 months) with low usage, no team invited, no workflow or report, and an open ticket saying the screen lacks the sidebar and create button. Needs an onboarding playbook and a plan/permission check.

ACC-0014.explanation: Healthy usage, clean billing and a long tenure. The departmental reorg email explicitly says no change to ownership or billing.

ACC-0015.explanation: Customer says a promised fix did not arrive and nobody wrote ('that's how trust gets lost'), and asks for honest roadmap status on custom fields. Trust is eroding even though usage and billing look fine.

ACC-0016.explanation: Usage is steady, billing clean, and the customer mentioned audit season busyness. Tickets are minor and closed.

ACC-0017.explanation: Weekly sessions fell steadily from about 98 to 22 over 12 weeks with no explanation in emails or notes. An integration-guide ticket has been open for 62 days, which may be a driver.

ACC-0018.explanation: Usage is up roughly 70% and the customer asked for a walkthrough for new department heads, saying they could use the platform more across the business. This is an expansion opportunity.

ACC-0019.explanation: Usage is steady, billing clean and tickets are routine. Reply to the pending call request on report ideas, but no risk signals.

ACC-0020.explanation: Sessions fell from about 27 to 7 over the period despite a 36-month tenure, with no CSM contact in 73 days. No explanation given, and an open mobile-approval ticket suggests unmet needs.

ACC-0021.explanation: Downgrade requested with an invoice 21 days overdue and a failed payment, but the open ticket shows their purchase order process needs a formal quote and payment by check. Usage is stable, so resolve the payment process.

ACC-0022.explanation: Invoice is 48 days overdue, and an open ticket says it bills five users when only three are active. Correcting the seat count should resolve the dispute; usage is stable but onboarding is incomplete.

ACC-0023.explanation: Sessions fell from 82 to 14 over 12 weeks, a steady decline with no explanation, and onboarding is incomplete (no team invited or workflows). The part-timer departure does not explain it.

ACC-0024.explanation: Usage has tripled and the customer got budget to expand and requested a proposal for procurement and inventory teams. A sales opportunity, with no CSM contact in 98 days.

ACC-0025.explanation: Stable usage, clean billing, positive feedback and only closed how-to tickets.

ACC-0026.explanation: Customer is angry that the export bug reported in March is still unfixed and says support is worse than the bug. Closed tickets did not resolve the issue, so the loss risk is real despite stable usage.

ACC-0027.explanation: Largest account ($1,960 MRR) with downgrade requested, an invoice 35 days overdue, and three open tickets including a seat-count billing dispute. Usage is healthy but a human should resolve billing and the downgrade.

ACC-0028.explanation: Usage dipped and is recovering, and the CSM note explains a year-end code freeze with reports still in use. Billing is clean and emails are positive.

ACC-0029.explanation: Their ops person resigned, the team is scrambling, and they asked to pause automated sends. Usage and billing are fine, but there has been no CSM contact for 97 days and a human should handle the request.

ACC-0030.explanation: Usage is steady, billing clean and feedback positive. An invoice-download ticket has been open for 69 days, so close it out.
